summary.name: Helix
summary.one_liner: Helix is a free, open-source, private macOS app for organizing, analyzing and graphing scientific data, positioned as an alternative to GraphPad Prism.
use_cases: Running t tests and ANOVA on lab measurements
Making publication-ready dose-response or survival curves
Creating volcano plots from gene data
Analyzing experimental data without sending it to the cloud
Replacing GraphPad Prism on a Mac
summary.what_it_does: Helix provides spreadsheet-like data tables in five types (column, XY, grouped, multiple variables, contingency) with copy-paste from Excel or Numbers. Statistical analyses run through R inside the app via webR, including t tests, ANOVA variants, nonparametric tests, multiple comparisons, correlation, linear and nonlinear regression, and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Each table keeps its own analyses and graphs, which update when data change. Graphs are built with Plotly and can be exported as PNG (150, 300 or 600 dpi), SVG or JPG.
notable: Runs R statistics inside the app via webR (R compiled to WebAssembly)
Project files (.hlx) are plain JSON documented openly
Built with Tauri rather than Electron; signed and notarized by Apple
Source code public on GitHub under GPL-3.0
caveats: Only macOS is named on the page; no Windows or Linux build is mentioned
Makes a daily check on GitHub for new versions, its only network connection
